TÜRKİYE · DAY-AHEAD OUTLOOK · 31 October 2026
Tomorrow's net load swing is narrower than the past month's median.

📉 Net load, once wind and solar are taken out of the load plan, is lowest at 12:00 at 23,371 MWh, while the evening reaches 39,627 MWh. The swing between them is 16,256 MWh, which is 5.2% narrower than the median swing of the 30 days from 30 September to 29 October 2026.

⚙️ LOWEST NET LOAD. 12:00 to 12:59 is the day's very low net load band. The lower of the Market Clearing Price (MCP) and the System Marginal Price (SMP) was at or below 150 TL/MWh in the 12:00 hour on 14 separate days from 30 September to 29 October 2026.

⚙️ HIGHEST NET LOAD. 17:00 to 21:59 is the day's very high net load band. The higher of MCP and SMP reached the 4,500 TL/MWh cap in 36 hours across 15 separate days in that window over the same dates.

🔎 WHAT STANDS OUT
Net load is at 36,433 MWh or higher in every hour of the very high band. The low band lasts one hour, the high band five.

💡 What it means: the plants that fill in after wind and solar have less ground to cover than on a typical day.

METHOD
📐 Net load = load plan − wind forecast − solar
🌞 Solar: no EPİAŞ forecast exists; shaped from the mean realised profile of 23 October to 29 October 2026 (7 complete days)
📊 Bands: quintiles of the look-back window, not of the target day

Source: EPİAŞ Transparency Platform, 30 October 2026

GREAT BRITAIN · DAY-AHEAD OUTLOOK · 31 October 2026
Wind opens at its strongest and reaches its low twice, the second time deeper.

📉 The wind trajectory for 31 October 2026, as published by the system operator:
The day opens at its highest reading, 5,194 MW at 00:00, and every step from 00:00→01:00 to 04:00→05:00 is a fall. The forecast stays low through the morning and early afternoon, with its lowest readings across 12:00 to 15:00, rises to a second high across 18:00 to 21:00, and closes at 3,345 MW at 23:00. The distance from the lowest reading to the highest is 2,365 MW.

⚙️ LOWEST WIND. 12:00-14:59, between 2,829 MW and 2,898 MW. No single lowest hour is named: 12:00, 13:00 and 14:00 in the block and 15:00 after it sit within 3% of one another. At least two of the day's three lowest readings fall in this block. The third place is open among a block hour and 15:00, 11:00, 05:00 and 06:00 outside it, which sit within 3% of 12:00; 10:00 sits more than 3% above 12:00.

⚙️ HIGHEST WIND. 00:00-02:59, between 3,853 MW and 5,194 MW. The day's three highest readings all fall in this block, at 00:00, 01:00 and 02:00 in that order, each more than 3% from the next. Every reading after 02:00 sits more than 3% below it.

🔎 WHAT STANDS OUT

The day has a second low. The opening fall stops at 05:00, at 2,947 MW; every step from 05:00→06:00 to 07:00→08:00 is a rise and every step from 08:00→09:00 to 13:00→14:00 is a fall, to readings at 13:00 and 14:00 that sit more than 3% below 05:00.

Between the lows the forecast never climbs more than 148 MW above the 05:00 reading, and the eleven readings from 05:00 to 15:00 span 266 MW. The lowest three-hour block sits on the later low and leaves 05:00 outside it.

METHOD
📐 Figures are the system operator's day-ahead wind forecast, in MW, read on the hour in local time
🌬️ Wind forecast is transmission-connected output only
🔌 Distribution-connected wind and solar are not metered by the system operator; they appear as reduced national demand rather than as generation
📊 Peak demand is published as a single daily figure, not a half-hourly curve

TÜRKİYE · DAY-END SCORECARD · 27 October 2026
Yesterday hydro carried the largest renewable share of Türkiye's power.

📊 The day's generation mix (EPİAŞ):
🌞 Solar 6.8% (licensed 1.1% + unlicensed 5.7%)
💧 Hydro (dams + rivers) 24.5%
🍃 Wind 13.4%
🔥 Natural gas only 17.8%
🌱 Total renewables 50.1% — all fossil 49.9%

📉 The price (MCP, Market Clearing Price):
🌙 02:00–05:00 → 2,700 TL/MWh, the floor of the day, with demand at 31,277 MWh at 04:00
🌙 17:00–18:00 → 4,500 TL/MWh, the ceiling of the day, with demand at 45,281 MWh at 17:00
Daily average 3,442 TL/MWh.

Between the solar peak at 11:00 and 17:00, the first hour at the ceiling, demand rose 91 MWh and solar (licensed + unlicensed) fell 9,491 MWh. Hydro, wind and other renewables added 4,626 MWh over the same hours, and fossil plants added 4,855 MWh.

⚡ Balancing cost 13,510,550 TL, measured as value against the day-ahead price. Of the 23,045 MWh instructed up and down, 3,185 MWh carried a constraint code. The costliest hour was 13:00, at 1,782,967 TL, an hour of up-regulation. On the published supply curve, buying that volume in the day-ahead market would have lifted the clearing price to the price cap, above that hour's System Marginal Price (SMP), so day-ahead buying would have cost more.

📆 Versus 26 October: wind output was up 48%, and the daily average price was flat against 3,436 TL/MWh.
📆 Versus 20 October, the same weekday one week earlier: wind output was up 552%, and the daily average price edged up from 3,297 TL/MWh.

💡 What it means:
A first reading: the 1,091 TL/MWh jump in the day-ahead price from 07:00 to 08:00, the day's largest hour-to-hour rise, is consistent with the morning demand ramp. Demand rose 6,221 MWh in that hour, more than solar (+2,728 MWh) and hydro, wind and other renewables (+1,098 MWh) added together, which left fossil plants 2,395 MWh more to cover.

At 11:00, both days short: £116.66/MWh on 27 October, £244.00/MWh on 26 October

📊 The day's generation mix (Elexon):
🍃 Wind 18,533 MW at 02:00, falling to 13,684 MW at 23:30
🔥 Natural gas 3,414 MW at 10:00, rising to 10,024 MW at 17:30
☀️ Solar peaked at 6,145 MW at 12:00 and was at zero from 17:30
💧 Pumped storage was at zero at 00:30 and peaked at 1,120 MW at 19:00
⚛️ Nuclear moved between 5,075 MW and 5,109 MW across the day
🏠 National demand 20,119 MW at 04:30, rising to 35,752 MW at 17:30
🔌 Interconnectors: net export of 2,226 MW at 06:00, net import of 746 MW at 12:00, 630 MW at 17:30 and 984 MW at 18:00

📉 The system price:
🌙 £16.98/MWh at 00:00
🌜 -£15.61/MWh at 06:00, the floor of the day
🌞 £280.13/MWh at 18:00, the ceiling of the day

Between 12:00 and 17:30 national demand rose by 10,581 MW, the largest change of any series. GB solar is almost all embedded, so its fall from the midday peak to zero sits inside that demand rise and is not a second need on top of it. Gas generation rose by 6,093 MW over the same half hours, wind fell by 2,208 MW and pumped storage rose by 895 MW, while nuclear barely moved and net interconnector import fell by 116 MW.

⚡ 13 half hours had NIV above zero (short), 1,741.8 MWh in total, and 35 had NIV below zero (long), 11,009.0 MWh in total. Accepted offers totalled 156,269.2 MWh and accepted bids 191,839.2 MWh over the day.

📆 Versus 26 October at 18:00: the price was £243.48/MWh against £280.13/MWh on 27 October, NIV 401.2 MWh against 527.4 MWh, and wind 18,745 MW against 15,453 MW.
📆 Versus 20 October at the same half hour, the Tuesday before: the price was £210.75/MWh against £280.13/MWh, NIV 472.3 MWh against 527.4 MWh, and wind 12,166 MW against 15,453 MW.

💡 What it means:
At 11:00 on 27 October 2026 the system price was set by offers from two units whose fuel the data lists as OTHER and as not listed, in a half hour short by 125.1 MWh, with national demand at 25,059 MW, solar at 5,909 MW and pumped storage at 236 MW. At the same half hour on 26 October 2026 it was set by offers from gas-fired plant (CCGT), in a half hour short by 494.7 MWh, with national demand at 34,137 MW, solar at 1,569 MW and pumped storage at 321 MW, and that price was the higher of the two. The fuel setting the price in a short half hour is not a fixed feature of the market: it was a different one at the same clock time on two consecutive days.

📈 System prices: Elexon Insights, 20, 26 and 27 October 2026

💧 Hydro (dams + rivers) 26.0%

⚡ Balancing cost 7,442,384 TL, measured as value against the day-ahead price. Of 26,606 MWh of instructed volume, 7,321 MWh was constraint-coded. At 20:00 the system called 1,241 MWh of up-regulation; on the published supply curve, buying that volume in the day-ahead market would have lifted the clearing price to 4,140 TL/MWh.

📆 Versus 25 October, a Sunday: the daily average price was 31.1% higher on 26 October, and the floor sat at 0 TL/MWh from 10:00 to 13:00 on 25 October against 03:00 on 26 October.

💡 What it means:
In Türkiye's power market, the morning build-up of solar goes hand in hand with lower output from hydro, wind and other renewables. On 26 October those plants produced 2,817 MWh less at 12:00 than at 07:00, a 19.3% drop, while solar (licensed + unlicensed) added 10,110 MWh, more than the 6,477 MWh increase in demand. The mornings of 25 October and 19 October followed the same pattern, with solar growing by more than demand and hydro, wind and other renewables ending lower at 12:00 than at 07:00.
